newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Storm Josephine nears Florida Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Josephine nears Florida Gulf Coast.

text.p: Tropical Storm Josephine drew closer to Florida's Gulf Coast Monday, and forecasters at the National Hurricane Center said they expected it to make landfall within a few hours.

At about 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT), Josephine's center was located near latitude 29.0 north and longitude 85.3 west or about 50 miles (80 km) south-southwest of Apalachicola, Fla., and moving northeast near 23 mph (37 kph). "On this track the center will cross the coast in the hurricane warning area during the next few hours," the National Hurricane Center said.

A hurricane warning was in effect from the Anclote Keys to Apalachicola, Fla. A tropical storm warning was in effect south of the Anclote Keys to Venice, Fla., and west of Apalachicola to Fort Walton Beach, Fla. A tropical storm warning also was in effect for the U.S. east coast from Cape Canaveral, Fla., north to Little River Inlet, S.C.

Maximum sustained winds remained near 70 mph (112 kph), keeping Josephine below hurricane strength of 74 mph (119 kph) and little significant change was expected before landfall, although forecasters noted that only a slight increase in wind speed would make Josephine a hurricane.
The storm was expected to weaken after moving inland.
Tropical storm force winds extended outward up to 175 miles (280 km) from Josephine's center. Rainfall amounts of five inches (12.5 cm) or more were possible along the storm's path.
Strong onshore winds were expected to cause coastal storm surge flooding of six to nine feet (two to three meters) or higher near and to the east of where the storm's center comes ashore.
Forecasters also warned of the possibility of tornadoes over northern and central Florida.
